title:
Approved,
Not Ashamed
paragraphs: Paul could have told Timothy to sharpen his delivery, read the room, win the crowd. Instead he tells him to study — because the only audience who will ever cross-examine his life is God, not the congregation watching him preach. Shame doesn't show up the day people stop clapping; it shows up the day you get called to account for work you never actually did. Approval earned alone, unseen, in a book nobody watched you open, will outlast applause from a room that forgets your name by Monday.

Most of us build our confidence out of reactions we can't control — a comment, a compliment, a crowd's mood on any given Sunday. But reactions are weather, and weather changes by the hour; approval built on weather will always leave you anxious. Rightly dividing the Word is work nobody sees you do, in rooms nobody claps in, and it's exactly the kind of work that leaves you unashamed on the day everyone else's performance finally gets exposed. Study now so you're not scrambling for an answer later.
